[iOS] Show Site Settings permission values as trailing text

Site Settings permission rows showed their current value (e.g. "Ask
first") as a subtitle. Show it as trailing text next to the disclosure
indicator instead, matching other Settings rows such as Search Engine.
VoiceOver now reads the value as the row's accessibility value, and the
rows get the button trait.

Handle reset of finished off-screen animations

We do not reset the compositing status if the reason for not running
on the compositor was solely due to having no visible effect. By not
resetting, we allow a native paint worklet to make a fresh compositing
recommendation once scrolled into the paint apron. The reset must
happen, however, if the previous recommendation was "composited".
Failure to mark as "needs repaint" can result in holding on to a stale
deferred paint image. This patch addresses the missing reset.

Fix BlitRGBAToYUVA() edge coverage on odd-sized subsampled targets

Subsampled planes of odd-sized images are allocated with ceiling-rounded
dimensions (via SkYUVAInfo::PlaneDimensions()), while dividing dst_rect
by nominal subsampling factors in float produces fractional bounds (e.g.
2047.5 on a 2048-texel plane). Non-AA draws with fractional right/bottom
edges do not rasterize the last column/row under standard half-open
rasterization rules, leaving edge texels unwritten even though callers
mark the destination SharedImage as fully cleared.

Round plane_dst_rect out to whole texels with roundOut() and clamp to
the plane surface bounds with intersect(). Also guard src_image before
querying isOpaque() to avoid a null pointer dereference when clearing to
black with nullptr source on multiplanar formats with alpha.

Add unit tests in RGBAToYUVATest.OddDimensionsSubsampled and
RasterDecoderOOPTest.CopySharedImageOddSizeMultiplanar.

[inline] Prewarm the selection overlay WebContents and adopt it on show

Booting the overlay WebUI only after the screenshot is captured delays
the overlay by about 270 ms.

Let SelectionOverlayPrewarmer load the WebUI in a detached WebContents
and hand it to the next session with the same interaction options, so
the page binds during capture. The prewarm is dropped after 10 s, on tab
switch, detach or close, or when its renderer goes away, and an error
page is never adopted. Its handler request is held until adoption; any
other unbindable request, or a second bind, is a bad message.

Since an adopted overlay is shown during capture, the page ignores
input, keeps the normal cursor and fills the viewport until its
screenshot is shown, and Esc closes it. Nothing triggers a prewarm yet.

Bug: b:575498249
Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter="SelectionOverlayPrewarmer*"
Test: browser_tests --gtest_filter="SelectionOverlayPrewarm*:SelectionOverlayBrowserTest.*CreatePageHandlerIsBadMessage:GlicSelectionOverlay*"

[TabBottomSheet] Lazily inflate WebViewResizingHelper placeholder

Previously, WebViewResizingHelper eagerly instantiated
ResizingPlaceholderCoordinator and attached the placeholder view in
reset() (invoked during setThinWebView()). This added view inflation and
layout overhead during bottom sheet setup even when resizing was never
initiated.

This CL defers resizing placeholder instantiation until resizing mode
is enabled:
- Defer creating ResizingPlaceholderCoordinator until resizing
        is requested via enableResizingMode().
- Cache visible height updates arriving before placeholder
        inflation and apply them once the coordinator is created.
- Ensure the resizing placeholder is inserted at index 0
        (beneath the ThinWebView in the FrameLayout) to preserve
        correct Z-order during alpha cross-fade animations.
- Update unit tests to verify that setThinWebView() and
        pre-resize height updates do not trigger coordinator
        instantiation.

[Voice Search] Scale simulated recording wave on Android

Currently, AudioProcessorService simulation mode is only enabled on
Android (including Desktop Android) via ComposeboxVoiceSearchElement,
while non-Android platforms read live microphone levels. Update
simulated volume handling for <recording-wave>:

- Raise simulated bump heights from 0.08-0.20 up to 0.45-0.85, add
  initial speech/transcript spikes, and slow per-frame decay to 0.9 so
  bumps visibly move <recording-wave>'s 8px-36px bars.
- Remove bezierEasing(0.4, 0.6), whose S-curve shrank volumes below 0.5
  (e.g., turning 0.20 into 0.09) and made bumps flatter instead of
  taller.
- Track syllable count instead of word count in triggerSyllableBumps()
  and stop skipping the first syllable so short words like "hi" and
  streaming partial words like "art" -> "artificial" still trigger
  bumps.
- Start new bumps at the current frame instead of 12 frames (~200ms) in
  the past so bumps are not already dying out before a bar spawns.
- Hold speech spikes in pendingSpikeAmplitude until the next getVolume()
  call (every 120ms) so mid-interval spikes do not decay before any bar
  sees them.
- Move the isListening check above receivedSpeech and transcript in
  RecordingWaveElement.updated() so initial speech updates are not
  ignored when Lit batches them together.

screencast/cast/NDgzMDM0OTQ1NTUyMzg0MHw0MmM3NzNhOS05Mg.

[base] Improve ApkAssets, VirtualDocumentPath, and MemoryConsumer JNI

Modernize JNI boundary types and reduce JNI calls in base/android:
- Annotate ApkAssets.open() with @JniType to convert
  std::vector<int64_t> directly via JNI Zero.
- Pass packed MemoryConsumerTraits as a primitive int across
  MemoryConsumerRegistration.Natives.register() instead of calling back
  into Java from C++ via Java_MemoryConsumerTraits_getPackedTraits(),
  saving a reverse JNI call per consumer registration.
- Clean up VirtualDocumentPath JNI string conversion.

[Public Transit] Clean up windows after AddressEditorRenderTest

Remove the skipWindowAndTabStateCleanup() opt-out.

The test set a mock last-used profile, left over from when the address
editor looked up the profile itself; the editor now receives it
explicitly. Closing the last tab during the test rule's cleanup opens
the hub, which requires a native-initialized last-used profile, so drop
the override. The mock IdentityServicesProvider is only reset after
the rules run, so let it serve any profile.

Validate upload URL scheme and origin in ResumableDriveUploader

In ResumableDriveUploader::HandleInitiationResponse(), the continuation
URL parsed from the X-Goog-Upload-URL header was previously only checked
for validity. This adds validation to ensure the URL uses the HTTPS
scheme and matches the origin of the Drive upload endpoint before
reading content or issuing chunk upload requests.

Also updates unit tests to verify that non-HTTPS or cross-origin
continuation URLs are rejected.

[SuperSize] Replace RE2 in Caspian StripNumbers and NormalizeStarSymbols

DiffHelper::StripNumbers and DiffHelper::NormalizeStarSymbols previously
invoked RE2::PartialMatch and RE2::GlobalReplace/RE2::Replace on every
unmatched symbol in matching passes 2 and 3, allocating multiple
temporary strings per symbol.

Replace both with single-pass ASCII scans and drop the RE2 dependency
from diff.cc.

Also extends TestStarSymbolNormalization so that NormalizeStarSymbols is
exercised in pass 3 (previously the test matched in pass 2).

WebUIToolbar: Fix BrowserFeaturePromoController interactive UI tests

When the WebUI toolbar is enabled, toolbar buttons such as
kToolbarAppMenuButtonElementId are hosted inside the toolbar WebView as
ui::TrackedElementWebUI instances rather than views::TrackedElementViews
instances, and ToolbarView::toolbar_controller() is null because
responsive overflow is managed by the WebUI toolbar in JavaScript.

This caused three sets of failures in
browser_feature_promo_controller_interactive_uitest.cc:
1. ShowCustomHelpBubble* crashed when casting the anchor element to
   views::TrackedElementViews in the TestCustomHelpBubbleView factory.
2. CustomActionCallbackInSecondWindow* crashed when looking up
   kToolbarAppMenuButtonElementId via BrowserElementsViews::GetView() to
   hide the first window's anchor.
3. PromoExemptFromToolbarNotCollapsed crashed on CHECK(controller) when
   collapsing the toolbar in the test.

Update the test helpers and fixtures in
browser_feature_promo_controller_interactive_uitest.cc to support both
Views and WebUI toolbar anchors and overflow.

Fixed tests:
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.CustomActionCallbackInSecondWindow
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.CustomActionCallbackInSecondWindowAfterFirstCloses
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble_Action
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble_Cancel
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble_Dismiss
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble_PressEsc
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerUiTest.ShowCustomHelpBubble_Snooze
- BrowserFeaturePromoControllerOverflowUiTest.PromoExemptFromToolbarNotCollapsed

[SuperSize] Use a flat index chain in Caspian MatchSymbols

MatchSymbols previously mapped each SymbolMatchIndex to a std::list of
symbol pointers, allocating and freeing a heap node for every symbol in
each matching pass, and invoked key_func through std::function.

Store duplicate-key chains in a flat next_in_bucket index vector with
inline head/tail indices in before_symbols_by_key, pre-reserve
before_symbols_by_key, and template MatchSymbols on KeyFunc.

Also adds a test where 3 "before" and 4 "after" symbols share a key, to
cover in-order pairing and an exhausted bucket.

MainThreadSchedulerImpl::OnTaskStarted invokes
PerformanceScenarioObserverList::NotifyAllScopes at the start of every
non-nested task on CrRendererMain, and SetScenarioValue invokes
NotifyIfScenarioChanged on CrBrowserMain. Previously, even when neither
LoadingScenario nor InputScenario had changed (>99.9% of tasks), each
NotifyAllScopes call re-acquired MappingPtrLockForScope 4 times, cloned
RefCountedScenarioMapping 4 times, and scanned 2 absl::flat_hash_map
pattern tables:
1. SetInitialScenarioState dropped initial_mapping after reading the
   initial values, forcing NotifyIfScenarioChanged and
   AddMatchingObserver to re-acquire MappingPtrLockForScope and clone
   RefCountedScenarioMapping on every lookup.
2. NotifyIfScenarioChanged unconditionally iterated
   matching_observers_by_pattern_ even when neither scenario changed and
   no newly added pattern was out of sync with last_*_scenario_.

Retain RefCountedScenarioMapping on PerformanceScenarioObserverList
under lock_ once initialized and skip matching_observers_by_pattern_
iteration when scenarios have not changed and all patterns are synced,
gated behind kOptimizePerformanceScenarioObserverNotify.

Create OWNERS file for Blink inputs.

During a recent security shepherding rotation, Sheepdog seemed to get
confused on a bug related to inputs, and attempted to assign the bug to
one of the many OWNERS in third_party/blink/renderer/OWNERS at random
instead of to a more appropriate, specific owner.

It seems reasonable to have an OWNER file in `input` (while still
leaving the human-readable file in third_party/blink/renderer/OWNERS),
as this would seem to add more clarity for bots and people alike.

(Let me know if this isn't right/appropriate; I'm wise in the ways of
security triaging but know little about blink itself!)

8fb9f184c24a7fdde1225cd3a6c714ab4c11ea05 [ diff ] 
[WebUI Toolbar] Support context menu on toolbar in vertical tabs mode

When the vertical tab strip is shown, the toolbar sits at the top of the
window and its empty space acts as the window caption: it supports
window dragging, double-click to maximize, and the system context menu
(which includes items such as pinning Gemini to the toolbar). The native
toolbar achieves this in IsPositionInWindowCaptionForView(), but the
WebUI toolbar is a single WebView, so the whole area was treated as an
interactive control and none of these worked.

Make the WebUI toolbar follow the same rule as the native toolbar:

- The WebUI declares the draggable area with the `app-region` CSS
  property. The document is draggable and the toolbar marks its children
  `no-drag`. The extensions and pinned actions containers opt back in to
  `drag` from their own styles, and their actions declare `no-drag`
  themselves, keeping the gaps and dividers between actions draggable,
  like the native ToolbarIconContainerView. The extensions container's
  hover outline uses `app-region: initial` so that it doesn't override
  the actions' `no-drag`.
- WebUIToolbarWebView stores the region reported by the renderer and
  exposes IsPositionInWindowCaption(). Since the region is only needed
  while the vertical tab strip is shown, ToolbarView enables collecting
  it only then. The region is reset when collection is disabled or the
  renderer goes away.
- IsPositionInWindowCaptionForView() delegates to the WebUI toolbar when
  the point is over it.

Since the result feeds the same non-client hit-test as the native
toolbar, dragging, double-click and the system menu are handled by the
existing platform paths on Windows, Mac and Linux.

gpu: Exclude Gfxstream and Lavapipe from Android Vulkan defaults

Starting in Android 37.2 (Mesa 26.3+), the Android emulator's guest
Gfxstream Vulkan ICD (vulkan.ranchu.so) reports driverID =
VK_DRIVER_ID_MESA_GFXSTREAM (29) in VkPhysicalDeviceDriverProperties
regardless of whether the host emulator uses SwiftShader
(-gpu swangle_indirect) or Lavapipe (-gpu lavapipe).

Because IsDefaultANGLEVulkan() previously only checked for
VK_DRIVER_ID_GOOGLE_SWIFTSHADER and VK_DRIVER_ID_MESA_LLVMPIPE,
Android 37.2 emulators inadvertently enabled the ANGLE Vulkan backend
on top of Gfxstream, leading to GPU process crashes in
rx::WindowSurfaceVk::swapImpl / NewFence (SurfaceVk.cpp:442) due to a
fence status caching issue in guest vulkan.ranchu.so.

Exclude VK_DRIVER_ID_MESA_GFXSTREAM in IsDefaultANGLEVulkan() so
Android emulators continue to use ANGLE's OpenGL ES backend, and also
exclude Mesa Lavapipe (vendor_id = 0x10005, device_id = 0x0) alongside
SwiftShader in CheckVulkanCompatibilities() on Android.

[SUIT] Shared C++ normalization for SuggestTemplateInfo

Introduce CreatePresentationTemplate() in components/omnibox/browser/ to
synthesize a complete SuggestTemplateInfo presentation template from an
AutocompleteMatch without mutating the underlying match.

Currently, desktop WebUI synthesizes presentation templates in its mojom
layer. This CL extracts the presentation synthesis logic (primary and
secondary text, classifications, swap handling, server color and a11y
preservation, placement, and image) into a shared C++ utility.

This enables cross-platform sharing of SUIT presentation logic across
surfaces. Mojo conversion in suggest_template_info_mojo_utils is updated
to use CreatePresentationTemplate() on demand (whenever a process
requests a normalized SuggestTemplateInfo for a match), ensuring
complete, non-null Mojo structs for WebUI rendering while preserving
server a11y_text.

[ChromeCompanero] Use DIR_MODULE on unbundled macOS test binaries

On macOS, GetLibraryPath() unconditionally resolved
libchromecompaneros.dylib via base::apple::FrameworkBundlePath(). In
unbundled test binaries such as unit_tests, ChromeTestSuite overrides
FrameworkBundlePath() to point to Google Chrome Framework.framework, so
scoping base::DIR_MODULE in
ChromeCompaneroHostTest.LibraryAbsentGracefulFailure still loaded the
packaged dylib from the framework bundle.

Check base::apple::AmIBundled() on macOS (matching
optimization_guide::GetSharedLibraryPath) so unbundled test binaries
resolve the library via base::DIR_MODULE, and use
base::GetNativeLibraryName("chromecompaneros") across platforms.

[Media] Track pending track changes in ffmpeg

Seeking during a track change can reallocate AVFormatContext::streams on
the blocking thread while an in-flight read completes on the media
thread, causing a potential UAF. To fix it:

 - Track pending track-change-inspired seek operations and their
   callbacks so that frame reads are paused
 - flush new streams immediately instead of waiting for seek completion
 - cache the time_base field so that CacheMetadataPacket doesn't try to
   access the streams from the media thread.

Expand content/SECURITY.md guidance on hypothetical observers

A recent wave of VRP reports claimed browser process use-after-frees
that only reproduce after injecting a deletion into browser code inside
an observer or delegate notification. The existing paragraph about
hypothetical observers already covers this, but triage, including
automated triage, still accepted these reports as high severity. In
several cases this happened after an earlier version of the same
report had been closed.

Give this guidance its own section and make it more explicit:
- Crash traces that need patched browser process code are not
  evidence, including when a closed report is resubmitted.
- A report must name the real code path. Being in the same class as a
  previously fixed bug is not enough.
- Destroying a WebContents while it notifies observers is already a
  safe CHECK crash.
- Native nested message loops don't run Chromium tasks, so
  RunLoop-based simulations don't show that a bug is reachable.

[Tab] Use scoped TraceEvents in TabImpl

Manual TraceEvent.begin()/end() pairs need a try/finally (or a "do not
early return" rule in initialize()) to keep slices balanced. Scoped
try-with-resources events guarantee the end without that bookkeeping. In
show()/hide() the trace resource is declared before the binding batch so
the batch still closes inside the slice. No behavior change.

[Voice Search] Add a new arm that only updates the model

The NTP voice search LE needs one more arm: same UI as the control
group (the legacy NTP voice search UI), but the updated speech model as
google.com voice search, so the model change can be measured on its
own.

Chrome sends the params that identify NTP voice search
(client=chrome-ntp, condition=search) only while
VoiceSearchCoherenceSearchbox is on, and that feature also turns on the
new voice search UI. Add a VoiceSearchCoherenceRealboxKeepLegacyUi param
to that feature: the params still go out, but the NTP keeps the legacy
UI. chrome://flags lists it as Arm 5. The model switch itself happens
on the speech service once it maps client=chrome-ntp to google.com's
recognizer.

[Read Aloud] Hide native entry points for unsupported languages

When native Read Aloud is enabled, isReadable() only checked whether the
page was distillable, so "Listen to this page" was shown on pages in
languages without voices (e.g. Korean) and playback then failed.

Check the native voice catalog for the tab's playback language in the
native branch of isReadable(). Translated pages use the translated
language, so the entry point appears once a page is translated to a
supported language. Also notify readability listeners when voices
become available so entry points re-evaluate.

Legacy Read Aloud behavior is unchanged.

Fall back to native updater UI on WebView2 runtime failures

Handle browser-process exit, main-renderer exit and unresponsiveness,
navigation failures, and script failures through a single deferred
native UI handoff. Use separate initialization and update timeout
timers, require rendering acknowledgments, and retain only the latest
pending update without extending an outstanding update's timeout.

Ignore late callbacks after fallback, cancellation or closure and
preserve the native UI message loop. Add recovery coverage without
starting WebView2 browser processes.

Avoid logging embedded navigation documents and propagate initial
controller put_Bounds failures through the creation result.

[Actor] Resolve TaskOptions.actuation_tab_id as an actor surface ID

Allow starting an actor task directly on a headless surface. Headless
surfaces do not have a tab, so they must be identified by their actor
surface ID. Today, task creation treats the initial target ID as a tab
ID, preventing a task from starting on a headless surface.

This CL updates the task creation path to read the initial target ID
as an actor surface ID directly.

- In CreateTaskImpl(), construct the ActorSurfaceHandle using
  FromRawValue() instead of converting from a TabHandle.

- In ActorKeyedServiceAdapter::StartTask(), treat TargetSurface.tab_id
  as an actor surface ID and validate it in ActorSurfaceRegistry
  before passing it through to TaskOptions.

While kUseTabHandleAsSurfaceHandle remains enabled (default), a tab's
surface ID equals its tab ID, so existing tab targets continue to work
as before.

[sandbox] Handle child thunk allocation failure

Interception thunk allocation can fail under system memory pressure. The
existing CHECK on commitment failure crashes the browser even though the
child has not been resumed.

Return a sandbox setup error for reservation and commitment failures so
the broker can terminate the suspended child and report launch failure
without taking down the browser.

[omnibox] Enable short suggest path for all clients by default

Following https://crrev.com/c/8666158, set the default value of the
OmniboxSuggestPathClient feature parameter to an empty string so that
all suggest clients use the short suggest path by default.

This is a no-op change because the previous
parameter value already listed all active Chrome suggest clients, setting it to an empty string simply
ensures any future clients also use the short suggest path without
requiring allowlist updates.

[GEiC] Support two-way assistant switching in Settings

This is a follow-up CL to crrev.com/c/8705243 that updates the Gemini
assistant switcher in Chrome Settings when a personal profile is
eligible for Gemini Enterprise via the `GeminiEnterpriseUrl` policy.

It adds the corresponding toggle to the Gemini in Chrome settings page
so that it's possible for the user to switch back after they've gone
from GEiC back to GiC the first time. It also updates the copy for
the settings and moves them to the bottom of each setting page.

Screenshot (GiC): http://screen/DHtmLjbTzf3zhvU

Fix ShadowRoot subtests in html-unsafe-external-scripts-async.html

`document.currentScript` is null when a classic `<script>` executes in a
shadow tree, causing `resources/slow.js` to throw a TypeError on
`document.currentScript.src` and time out in the `ShadowRoot` subtests.

Rename `slow.js` to `slow.sub.js` and read the subtest `id` via WPT
server-side substitution (`{{GET[id]}}`) instead, preserving cross-test
isolation while allowing all `ShadowRoot` subtests to pass.

[iOS] Deduplicate Tips Magic Stack engagement metrics per impression

Actionable Tips cards (NTP Theme and Tips Notifications) allow multiple
in-place interactions without immediately dismissing the card.
Previously, each inline interaction logged the common engagement
metrics, inflating CTR compared to informational Tips cards that dismiss
on the first tap.

This CL ensures the common Tips and Magic Stack engagement signals are
recorded at most once per card impression across both informational and
actionable variations.

[ios] Add LocationBarBadgeTabHelperObserverBridge

Objective-C UI components and mediators (such as
LocationBarBadgeMediator) observe LocationBarBadgeTabHelper via an
Objective-C protocol.

Introduces LocationBarBadgeTabHelperObserverBridge, a bridge pattern
implementation that connects LocationBarBadgeTabHelper C++ observation
to the LocationBarBadgeTabHelperObserving Objective-C protocol using
base::ScopedObservation. Destruction of the bridge cleanly
disconnects the observer without leaking pointers.

This is CL 3/4 in the Location Bar Badge TabHelper architecture stack.

Chain order: 3/4
Landing order: 3

ttc: Enforce enterprise policy checker on actor tasks and screenshots

TTC created its actor tasks with the null EnterprisePolicyChecker and
checked get_screenshot URLs without one, so enterprise policy never
applied to TTC actuation or screenshots. Pass TtcKeyedService's
ActorEnterprisePolicyChecker to both, as Glic and TTC's page context
monitor already do.

With the real checker, TTC actuation and screenshots follow the Glic
enterprise policies: URLs blocked by GlicActuationOnWebBlockedForURLs
are rejected, and on managed browsers or enterprise accounts every URL
is blocked unless GlicActuationOnWeb (or the enterprise default) allows
it. Text typed into pages also goes through DLP content validation.

Remove the IsUrlSupportedForPageContext() overload that skipped
enterprise policy; get_screenshot was its only caller.

Disable kPdfOpaqueOrigin in PDF partial-loading tests

With kPdfOpaqueOrigin, the PDF document commits an opaque origin, and
this causes issues for the PDF partial loading features
(kPdfPartialLoading, kPdfIncrementalLoading). The PDF plugin's range
requests to the PDF URL use the PDF URL as their referrer [1], and their
initiator is derived from that referrer [2], so it's the PDF URL's
origin. That doesn't match the opaque origin that the PDF frame's
URLLoaderFactory is locked to. The network service treats this as a bad
request initiator (see network::VerifyRequestInitiatorLock()) and kills
the renderer.

Partial loading has been disabled by default since 2020
(https://crbug.com/40123601), so this is not a blocker for enabling
kPdfOpaqueOrigin by default. To keep test coverage for partial loading
once kPdfOpaqueOrigin is enabled by default, explicitly disable
kPdfOpaqueOrigin in the two test fixtures that enable partial loading.
The TODO describes how to fix this if partial loading is ever turned
back on.

[1]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:pdf/loader/document_loader_impl.cc;l=321;drc=4002660cc2dd47891e14fba749e837d0904887ab
[2]
https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/web_associated_url_loader_impl.cc;l=416-426;drc=4002660cc2dd47891e14fba749e837d0904887ab

Add pdf_frame_util::GetPdfOrigin() and use it in PdfContentFetcher

With kPdfOpaqueOrigin (added in https://crrev.com/c/8544640), the PDF
content frame will commit an opaque origin as an implementation detail
of PDF isolation. This might break expectations for any features that
look at the PDF content frame's origin directly. In the current code,
only one feature was found to be affected: Glic PDF annotation looks at
the PDF content frame's origin directly. Such features really want to
know where a PDF came from rather than the opaque origin.

Add pdf_frame_util::GetPdfOrigin(), which returns the origin committed
by the PDF's placeholder document: the frame that navigated to the PDF
URL and embeds the PDF viewer. Its origin is what the content frame
would have had without kPdfOpaqueOrigin. It supports both the OOPIF and
GuestView PDF viewers by walking from the PDF extension frame with
GetParentOrOuterDocumentOrEmbedder(). GetPdfOrigin() is scoped to the
PDF viewer: for other PDF content frames, such as Print Preview's
chrome-untrusted://print frame, it falls back to the content frame's own
origin, which is opaque under kPdfOpaqueOrigin. None of the current
callers need Print Preview's PDF origin. Use
pdf_frame_util::GetPdfOrigin() in PdfContentFetcher, which reports the
PDF's origin to Glic via PdfResult::origin / PdfDocumentData.origin.

Note that an alternative approach is to reconstruct the origin from the
opaque origin's precursor. That approach was not pursued because it
can't distinguish from cases where the PDF truly came from an opaque
origin (such as when loaded from a data: URL).

[GEiC] Disable Chrome Skills for Gemini Enterprise profiles

Chrome Skills (`chrome://skills` and Glic skill invocation) is a
consumer Gemini feature and isn't supported in Gemini Enterprise (GEiC).

Adds `GlicFeature::kSkills`, supported by consumer Gemini and not by
Gemini Enterprise (`GlicProviderSpec::SupportsFeature()`), and gates:
- `SkillsServiceFactory::IsSkillsEnabledForProfile()`, disabling Glic
  skill invocation, UI controllers, and browser actions/commands;
- `showSkillsSettingPage` in `chrome://settings/ai`;
- `chrome://skills` (`isSkillsSupported` in `SkillsUI`), displaying an
  unsupported error page (`ErrorType.UNSUPPORTED`) with a link to
  manage skills in Gemini Enterprise (`/home/cid/<configId>/r/skills`
  or `/r/skills`).

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aKniaUSJehg5gZq6vTzNL3tJ-EhIvcAX/view

[iOS][VoiceSearch] Handle Voice Plate results in the composebox

This CL handles Voice Plate queries in the composebox by making
ComposeboxInputPlateCoordinator the delegate of the Voice Plate it
presents. Recognized queries are sent through the composebox with the
new -sendVoiceSearchQuery:, which marks the resulting navigation, if
any, as a Voice Search result (used by the NTP metrics). When the user
taps "Stop" to edit the query, it replaces the text in the focused
composebox omnibox.

The caller of these delegate methods will be added in an internal CL.

e82db535c8fd2b679ca5f4ef8a8d4ad54b5c4b59 [ diff ] 
IDB: add metrics to determine ideal db close grace period in SQLite

LevelDB is unaffected.

ConnectionDestructionGracePeriodWasUseful logs a binary result for
whether the destruction grace period successfully allowed a subsequent
connection to reuse a hot DatabaseConnection.

ConnectionReopenedAfterDestruction tells us how long it's been since the
database was last open. (Nothing is logged if it wasn't previously
opened.) This gives us an understanding of how much longer than 2s we'd
have to extend the grace period to capture more reopen cases.

Aside from collecting data, there are two slight behavioral changes:

1. In-memory DBs are closed (or not) without using the grace period
   (this frees memory slightly faster after an in-memory db is deleted)
2. An empty backing store is kept around for a full 3 minutes for
   SQLite, which should have little to no functional impact since the
   backing store doesn't hold onto files or much in the way of memory.
   This is necessary for the new metrics to work.

Restrict PVT explicitly to the Default Search Engine

This change introduces a restriction to the PVT feature. PVTs
are restricted to the user's actively selected Default Search
Engine (DSE).

Previously, the service evaluated token issuance solely against
anti-abuse configurations. Now, the service also strictly matches the
issuer's origin against the current TemplateURLService's default search
provider.

Key modifications:
- Updated PrivateVerificationTokensService to depend on
  TemplateURLService.
- Added IsSearchEngineSameOrigin and IsIssuerAllowed methods to enforce
  the identical origin constraint before tokens are fetched, stored, or
  redeemed.
- Configured TemplateURLService dynamically in browser tests to match
  the test server's ephemeral issuer origin, verifying full end-to-end
  resolution without requiring testing bypass flags.
- Migrated unit tests and URL loader throttle tests to instantiate and
  inject TemplateURLServiceFactoryTestUtil, dynamically mocking test
  domains as the default search engine, preventing regressions.

parent
6a30ecfb3a4da5dd6607bbb3a76500e066adc1be [ diff ] 
omnibox: Let the full WebUI popup adopt another window's WebContents

The classic and AI Mode presenters create their content through
CreateWebUIContent(), which can also wrap a WebContents that another
window released (crrev.com/c/8678826). The full WebUI popup sets its
content directly in its constructor, so its WebContents cannot move
between windows.

Create the full popup's content through CreateWebUIContent() as well,
still eagerly from the constructor, and give
OmniboxFullPopupWebUIContent a constructor that adopts a released
WebContents. OmniboxPopupWebUIContent no longer requires subclasses that
set their own URL to load a new WebContents.

No behavior change: the full popup doesn't join the per-profile pool
(crrev.com/c/8695085) yet, so nothing moves it. Creating it on omnibox
focus and sharing it across windows come in follow-ups.

[CSD] Capture the page for image embedding when no image is retained

Browser-side image embedding previously required a retained image from
visual classification. When visual classification is skipped (e.g. for
non-page-load triggers), Enhanced Protection pings lacked embeddings and
visual features.

Update `StartBrowserSideImageEmbedding()` to capture a screenshot on
demand via `CaptureScreenshot()` when no image is retained.

ozone/drm: Extend DRM authentication timeout to 30s

Previously, kMaxAuthAttempts was 50 (~5s). On cold boot, when frecon's
splash screen and hotplug rescans held DRM master past 5s (e.g. ~8.3s
observed on Chromeboxes with external displays), Chrome proceeded with
an unauthenticated primary FD and could not acquire DRM master later via
drmSetMaster() without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

Increase kMaxAuthAttempts to 300 (~30s). This gives >3x margin over the
observed frecon hold time (with no extra delay once master is released)
while staying well below session_manager's 60s browser hang-detection
abort threshold if retries are exhausted on GPU process restart.

installer: Snapshot --installerdata into setup's temp dir

When an install takes longer than the updater's kWaitForAppInstaller,
the updater stops waiting and deletes the --installerdata file while
setup.exe is still running. Setup then fails to write
initial_preferences and passes a missing file to the shortcut child,
silently dropping the initial preferences.

Copy the file into setup's own temp dir right after creating it and use
the copy from then on. If the copy fails, keep the original path.

[Tab] Factor native-page liveness and deferred-freeze helpers in TabImpl

The "native page is set and not frozen" check on mNativePage was
repeated inline across freeze/detach/show/hide paths, and the deferred
detached-NativePage freeze predicate and listener setup were inlined in
detachFromWindow(), making that method hard to follow. These are now
hasLiveNativePage(), shouldDeferDetachedNativePageFreeze() and
registerDetachedNativePageFreezeListener(). No behavior change:
getter-based checks (isNativePage()/getNativePage()), which are
overridden in tests, are intentionally left as-is.

Add BrowserAgentInfo to EventInitiatorInfo in browser_events.proto

Enterprise security events can already record that an extension, an
external CDP client or the DevTools UI was acting on the target tab.
Add a fourth initiator for in-browser AI agents, starting with Gemini
in Chrome, so admins can tell when an agent rather than the user
performed an action such as a login.

BrowserAgentInfo carries the agent type, the ID of the agent task that
was controlling the tab, and the conversation ID when the agent has
one. It has the lowest precedence in the EventInitiatorInfo oneof: it
is set only when no extension, CDP client or DevTools UI initiator
applies.

Nothing populates the field yet. Follow-up CLs will set it behind the
kEnterpriseGlicActorAttribution feature, which is disabled by default.

Fold Android.extras.bp.template into gen_android_bp.py

Previously, run_gn2bp.py generated a separate Android.extras.bp file by
performing raw string substitution on
components/cronet/gn2bp/templates/Android.extras.bp.template and
including it from the top-level Android.bp via `build =
["Android.extras.bp"]`. Because those modules lived in a raw text
template outside the Soong AST, gen_android_bp.py could not inspect or
manipulate them programmatically, requiring their referenced file paths
to be duplicated in COPYBARA_ADDITIONAL_PATHS and preventing them from
being dynamically derived from GN metadata.

This CL folds the modules from Android.extras.bp.template directly into
the top-level Blueprint AST:
- Add `create_extras_modules()` in gen_android_bp.py (and move
  `generate_libcronet_libcrypto_symbol_linker_script` into
  `setup_libcrypto_stripping()`) to emit these targets as first-class
  `soong_ast.Module` objects in the root Android.bp.
- Extend `soong_ast.py` with `android_library` support and `manifest`,
  `lint`, and `java_version` attributes on `JavaModule`.
- Teach `extract_copybara_paths()` to inspect `manifest` and
  `license_text` attributes and normalize Soong `/**/*` globs to
  Copybara `/**` globs, removing the need to hardcode paths referenced
  by those modules in `COPYBARA_ADDITIONAL_PATHS`.

[ios] Add priority arbitration and navigation lifecycle to LocationBarBadgeTabHelper

Location bar badge presentation on iOS requires deterministic
arbitration when multiple features request active badges simultaneously,
as well as clean lifecycle management across web navigations.

Introduces LocationBarBadgePriority tiers (kLow, kDefault, kHigh,
kCritical) and implements std::max_element priority arbitration in
LocationBarBadgeTabHelper. Tie-breaking between equal-priority badges is
resolved by arrival timestamp. On cross-document navigations,
non-persistent badges are cleared via std::erase_if while persistent
badges (such as Incognito) survive. All badge arbitration is guarded
under kLocationBarBadgeMigration.

This is CL 2/4 in the Location Bar Badge TabHelper architecture stack.

Chain order: 2/4
Landing order: 2

[ash] graduation: read the managed state off the User

GraduationManagerImpl asked the active user's Profile for its
ProfilePolicyConnector only to call IsManaged(). The user_manager::User
behind that Profile carries the same answer in User::is_managed(),
which UserCloudPolicyManagerAsh sets when the user's policy loads and
ProfileUserManagerController sets to false for users without policy,
both before the session starts.

Look the User up through BrowserContextHelper and read the state off
it. This drops the //chrome/browser/policy dependency from
chrome/browser/ui/ash/graduation.

Generate a file-exact Copybara origin list from GN and Soong AST

Previously, copy.bara.sky imported entire top-level and component
directory trees via broad globs (`base/**`, `build/**`, `crypto/**`,
`ipc/**`, `net/**`, `testing/**`, `url/**`, `COMPONENTS_PATHS`, and
`THIRD_PARTY_PATHS`). Importing whole directory trees pulled in
thousands of unused files into AOSP and required maintaining a large set
of ad-hoc directory exclusion rules in copy.bara.sky.

This CL switches gn2bp to generate an exact list of required origin
files and minimal data/resource globs in
`out/gn2bp/copybara_generated_paths.bara.sky`, reducing the number of
imported files by ~60%:
- Extend `extract_copybara_paths()` in `gen_android_bp.py` to collect
  exact file paths from the parsed GN graph (`sources`,
  `public_headers`, `inputs`, `crate_root`, `script`, JNI sources) and
  generated Soong modules (`srcs`, `tool_files`, `jars`,
  `linker_scripts`, `version_script`, `jarjar_rules`, `test_config`,
  `license_text`, and `Android.bp` files).
- Transitively scan C/C++ source and header files for `#include` /
  `#import` directives resolved against the target `include_dirs` so
  headers omitted from GN `sources` lists are automatically included.
- Extract `README.chromium` and associated license files (`LICENSE`,
  `METADATA`, `MODULE_LICENSE_*`) for all directories with generated
  modules.
- Emit exact file paths (`GENERATED_ORIGIN_FILES`) separately from
  wildcard globs (`GENERATED_ORIGIN_GLOBS`) and concatenate
  `GENERATED_ORIGIN_FILES` as a plain list in `copy.bara.sky` so
  Copybara uses `SequenceGlob` (O(1) hash-set lookup) instead of
  compiling thousands of regex path matchers.

Validate ComputedStyle state during animation keyframe resolution

StyleResolver::ComputeValue() constructs a StyleResolverState, which
traverses the flat tree and can synchronously trigger slot assignment
recalculation. If an element becomes unslotted during this traversal, it
is detached from the flat tree and its ComputedStyle is cleared.
Previously, StyleResolver::ComputeValue() cached
element->GetComputedStyle() before constructing StyleResolverState, and
animation curve helpers assumed GetComputedStyle() and computed values
remained non-null across the call.

Re-fetch and validate element->GetComputedStyle() after
StyleResolverState construction in StyleResolver::ComputeValue(), and
add null and style state checks in CompositorAnimationCurve,
CompositorAnimationColorCurve, ClipPathPaintDefinition, and
NativePaintWorkletData to avoid updating or recreating animation curves
on detached elements or mid-recalc states.

TAG=agy

- Update ReadAndValidateVectorSize to use PickleIterator::ReadLength and
  account for base::Pickle's 4-byte alignment when checking
  RemainingBytes().
- Use ReadAndValidateVectorSize in ReadResourceRequestBody instead of
  ReadInteger.
- Stop the vector deserialization loops in ReadU16StringVector,
  ReadResourceRequestBody, and ReadLegacyFrameState once parse_error is
  set. (A follow-up CL will replace DeserializeObject::parse_error with
  early returns via std::optional / base::expected.)

[RPS] Add per-actor chrome://flags options and remove testing params

With Search Agent now gated by its own
kRemoteActorCredentialSharingSearch feature and configured via
search_config_json, the temporary GWS testing variation in
chrome://flags and the legacy testing parameters on
kRemoteActorCredentialSharing are obsolete.

- Switches chrome://flags/#remote-actor-credential-sharing to
  MULTI_VALUE_TYPE with 'Enabled' (Gemini and Search), 'Enabled (Gemini
  only)', and 'Enabled (Search only)' options, removing
  kRemoteActorCredentialSharingGwsForTesting.
- Removes legacy override parameters (actor_name_for_testing,
  allowed_host_for_testing, allowed_host_actor_for_testing, and
  oauth_client_id) from kRemoteActorCredentialSharing in favor of
  gemini_config_json, search_config_json, and compiled-in per-actor
  defaults.
- Deduplicates the default Gemini OAuth client ID and task namespace ID
  fallback in RemoteActorCredentialPermissionClient via
  GetRemoteActorConfig(RemoteActorType::kGemini).

[UnboundedElement] Show renderer cursor over macOS unbounded surfaces

Previously, UnboundedSurfaceWindowMac ignored renderer cursor updates
because RenderWidgetHostViewMac::DisplayCursor only updated the main
RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa view, whose tracking area does not cover the
separate unbounded surface NSWindow.

This change:
* Adds a virtual DisplayCursor(const ui::Cursor&) method to
  UnboundedSurfaceWindow and overrides it in UnboundedSurfaceWindowMac
  so RenderWidgetHostViewMac can forward cursor updates without
  downcasting.
* Exposes -[RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa canChangeCurrentCursor] to share
  its keyTrackingWindow, _cursorHidden, and _showingContextMenu checks
  with UnboundedNSView.
* Tracks whether the pointer is inside the unbounded surface via an
  NSTrackingArea on UnboundedNSView, refreshes pointer-inside state from
  NSEvent.mouseLocation when SetBounds() moves or resizes the window
  under a stationary cursor, and applies the current NSCursor on mouse
  enter/move, cursor updates, and bounds changes when allowed.
* Resets the cursor to arrowCursor on mouse exit and window teardown
  only when shouldChangeCurrentCursor holds.

[glic] Implement Desktop Views support for GlicToast

GlicToast was originally added as an Android-only helper wrapping
MessageDispatcherBridge so Glic features could show a spark-branded
message banner. Callers that run across platforms still had to worry
about platform-specific toast APIs on Desktop Views.

This change turns GlicToast into a cross-platform interface taking a
TabInterface reference and splits the platform implementations into
glic_toast_android.cc (using MessageDispatcherBridge) and
glic_toast_impl.cc (using ToastController on Desktop Views). On Desktop,
a new ToastId::kGlic specification is registered with the Glic spark
icon and close button, formatting the title and optional description
into a single-line toast via IDS_GLIC_TOAST_TITLE_AND_DESCRIPTION.

[contextual-tasks] Show a contextual cue on return from a search

Adds AbaSearchJourneyCueTarget, a contextual cue that offers to reopen
the Search AI answer in the Contextual Tasks side panel when the user
returns to the tab they searched from (Tab A).

- The cue is generated locally: "See your Google AI search answer on
  this tab", with an "Open side panel" button. Clicking it calls
  RestoreJourneyInSidePanel().
- It's eligible while SearchJourneyTabFeature can restore the journey
  and the Contextual Tasks panel isn't open. It shows at most once per
  journey.
- Cues are only evaluated when a page loads, so when the user returns
  to Tab A, the target asks the tab's ContextualCueingController to
  evaluate it alone, with EvaluateCueForTarget().
- Tab features register the target when contextual cueing and
  kABASearchJourneys are on. Showing it also needs
  kContextualCueingV2MultiSource.

The cue shares the cueing framework's limits: a loud ABA cue starts the
backoff for every cue type, and their backoffs block it.

It can't show until Tab B's results page registers restore parameters
through registerAimThreadForPromo (crrev.com/c/8666408). A follow-up
hides the cue when its journey ends.

[grid-lanes] Coordinate column fragmentation breaks across spanners

Build on independent per-lane break handling to coordinate breakpoints
and break-after values across all lanes a spanner occupies. Honor early
breaks before or inside a spanner even when another lane selected the
breakpoint.

Persist break-before tokens for deferred items so spanners and following
content resume correctly without repeating completed items.

WPT's are added that exercise fragmentation across spanner boundaries.

[Linux] Move child processes into the XDG portal systemd scope

SetSystemdScopeUnitNameForXdgPortal() creates app-<name>-<pid>.scope
with only the browser PID. It runs after the zygotes, the GPU process,
renderers and utility processes have been spawned, so those stay in
the scope of whatever launched the browser (e.g. a terminal's
vte-spawn-*.scope or GNOME's app-gnome-*.scope). When that scope stops
(the terminal tab closes, or the session ends), systemd kills them
while the browser process keeps running. GPU process relaunches then
fail through the dead zygote until the browser crashes in
IntentionallyCrashBrowserForUnusableGpuProcess().

Create the scope with Delegate=true and, once it is active, scan /proc
on a thread pool sequence with base::ProcessIterator for descendants
that are still in a different cgroup and attach them with
AttachProcessesToUnit(), one PID at a time (StartTransientUnit fails
entirely with ESRCH if any listed process has exited). Parents are
attached before their children so that processes forked by the zygotes
inherit the new scope, and the scan is repeated (at most 3 passes) to
pick up processes forked during the migration. If
AttachProcessesToUnit() is unavailable (systemd older than v238), the
behavior is unchanged.

Tested by launching chrome with
`systemd-run --user --scope --unit=launcher.scope` and stopping that
scope after startup: before, all child processes stayed in
launcher.scope and the browser crashed ("GPU process launch failed:
error_code=1002"); after, all processes are in
app-org.chromium.Chromium-<pid>.scope and the browser survives.

[fuchsia] Decouple Cast web data directory from data quota setting

SetDataParamsForMainContext previously required data-quota-bytes to be
explicitly specified in config.json before creating /cache/web_profile
and configuring the data directory for the main Cast application
context. When data-quota-bytes was omitted to let WebEngine rely on
filesystem storage stats (statvfs) instead of recursive directory tree
traversals, the early return bypassed data directory initialization
entirely, causing WebInstanceHost to launch the context in incognito
mode without persistent web storage.

Matching the CDM storage setup, persistent data directory creation and
transfer should always occur for the main context, with
data-quota-bytes remaining an optional constraint if specified in
configuration.

Use fake fullscreen on Mac in remaining flaky fullscreen tests

AppMenuFullscreenInteractiveTest, WCODisabledInMacFullscreen, and
WindowSetResizableDoNotBlockFullscreenWebAPI check menu, Window Controls
Overlay, and resize gating behavior while fullscreen, rather than the
AppKit Space transition itself. On Mac bots, real AppKit fullscreen
transitions are slow and can stall or fail when windows compete for
focus, leaving FullscreenWaiter to time out.

Move ScopedFakeNSWindowFullscreen to AppMenuFullscreenInteractiveTest so
all app menu fullscreen tests share it, and add it to the two web app
frame toolbar fullscreen tests on Mac.

Remove UNSAFE_TODO() from base/i18n/file_util_icu.cc

In GetNextCodePoint(), pass *file_name instead of file_name->data() to
U16_NEXT() and U8_NEXT() so string indexing uses operator[]. This
removes the need for UNSAFE_TODO() around U16_NEXT(). For U8_NEXT(),
replace UNSAFE_TODO() with UNSAFE_BUFFERS() and a SAFETY comment since
U8_NEXT() internally indexes into 16-byte lookup table literals.

Also switch length() calls to size() since they mean the same thing.

This CL is AI generated.

[Linux] Support a substitute proc_dir in base::ProcessIterator

Add Linux/ChromeOS/Android proc_dir overloads to base::ProcessIterator,
base::GetProcessExecutablePath(), base::internal::GetProcPidDir(),
base::internal::ReadProcFile(), and base::internal::ReadProcStats() so
callers and unit tests can enumerate processes from a substitute procfs
directory instead of "/proc". Guard non-"/proc" paths with
CHECK_IS_TEST() so production callers only read from "/proc".

committed as an editable SVG source plus a PNG render of the same name
in the same directory. Add a presubmit error that fires when a
documentation SVG under //ios is added or modified without its PNG also
being added or modified. The error lists, per file, the exact command
that regenerates the PNG so that developers and agentic tools can fix
it mechanically.

The check only applies to SVGs with positive evidence of being doc
diagrams: a same-named PNG already sits next to the SVG, or a Markdown
file in its directory or parent directory references it by file name.
App asset SVGs have neither and are never flagged. As a backstop, SVGs
in .xcassets asset catalogs and ios/third_party are always exempt.

Simulating a CL that modifies all 88 SVGs under //ios flags only the 3
ios/architecture diagrams.

a6dae2dea8d9e1508f120b17ca784ec4fd145ee4 [ diff ] 
[Glic] Allow windowless ContinueActuationRequest on Android

When the experimental triggering coordinator has no prepared tab and
no browser window for the profile, it rejects the request with
kNoBrowserWindow.

On Android, Chrome can run a background task with no browser window: a
background trigger runs its first turn in an offscreen tab, and no
activity may exist. The first turn works because it gets a prepared tab,
but every follow-up continuation for that conversation is rejected, even
though the conversation's offscreen tab is still alive.
OpenEmptyWindow() is not supported on Android.

This CL:
1. On Android only, lets a ContinueActuationRequest proceed without a
   browser window when its conversation still has a live surface, so
   LastActiveOrNew resolves to that surface. A new HasLiveSurface()
   accessor on GlicInstance exposes this. If the conversation is unknown
   or its surface is gone, the existing kNoBrowserWindow rejection is
   unchanged, so the request still fails synchronously instead of
   failing later with kTabClosed. Desktop behavior is unchanged.
2. Sets auto_submit_options.show_panel = false on Android for
   continuations while Chrome is in the background (matching
   prepared_tab).
3. Adds unit tests for both platforms.

[Android] Guard tab discard on graceful shutdown

Under TabAndroidGracefulShutdown, closing a tab whose renderer cannot
fast-shut down detaches its WebContents into TabWebContentsDestroyer for
up to 2 seconds while retaining PageType::kTab. If swap-pressure tab
discard selects that PageNode, AttemptFastKillForDiscard synchronously
terminates the renderer, causing TabWebContentsDestroyer to delete the
WebContents before PageDiscarder::DiscardPageNode calls
contents->Discard().

Exclude WebContents-backed PageNodes lacking a TabInterface in
SwapPressureDiscardingPolicyAndroid so detached closing tabs and non-tab
ThinWebViews are neither counted toward the live-tab floor nor
discarded, and re-check the WebContents WeakPtr after
AttemptFastKillForDiscard in PageDiscarder::DiscardPageNode.

Validation: PageDiscarderFastKillTest.HandlesWebContentsDestroyedDuringFastKill
failed 3/3 without this change, passed 3/3 with it on
android_36_google_apis_x64_local

Add a static GlicEnabling check that says whether a profile can see the

open the panel in native FRE mode for eligible profiles.

crrev.com/c/8667669, without the HostCapability, and uses the
kGlicNativeFreAndroid flag that already landed.

[endpoint_fetcher] Support configuring RedirectMode on RequestParams

EndpointFetcher constructs a network::ResourceRequest and executes it
with SimpleURLLoader, attaching an OAuth2 Authorization Bearer header
for OAUTH-authenticated callers. Today, EndpointFetcher::RequestParams
does not expose a way to configure ResourceRequest::redirect_mode, so
all requests use the default RedirectMode::kFollow.

Browser-process callers that send OAuth Bearer tokens to fixed API
endpoints often want to disallow HTTP redirects (RedirectMode::kError)
so that a 3xx response fails immediately rather than following a
redirect with the Authorization header attached.

This CL adds an optional redirect_mode field and SetRedirectMode()
builder method to EndpointFetcher::RequestParams and wires it to
resource_request->redirect_mode when creating the SimpleURLLoader.

Allow TabCloseType.ALL as a no-op on StubTabModel

Many production cleanup paths (e.g., MultiInstanceManagerApi31,
terminateIncognitoSession, enforceIncognitoForcedPolicy,
CloseAllTabsHelper) and test tearDown helpers unconditionally call
getTabRemover().closeTabs(TabClosureParams.closeAllTabs()...) on both
TabModels in a TabModelSelector.

Update StubTabModel.closeTabs() and StubTabModel.getTabRemover() to
no-op when tabClosureParams.tabCloseType == TabCloseType.ALL (consistent
with EmptyTabModel and StubTabModel.setActive(false)), while continuing
to throw UnsupportedOperationException for SINGLE/MULTIPLE tab closures
and removeTab(). This eliminates the need for instanceof StubTabModel
guards across closeAllTabs() callers.

Also restrict TabBottomSheetManagerTest#testBottomSheetHiddenOnIncognito
to PHONE, since incognito uses separate single-profile windows on
tablets when EnforceIncognitoIsolation is enabled.

Re-enable WebUI omnibox in OmniboxViewViewsPlaceholderTest

OmniboxViewViewsPlaceholderTest disabled kWebUIOmniboxPopup and
kWebUIOmniboxAimPopup as a temporary workaround when the features were
enabled by default (https://crrev.com/c/8092074).

The fixture mocks the AIM eligibility service as eligible, so with
kWebUIOmniboxAimPopup enabled, omnibox::IsAimPopupEnabled() is true and
the default search engine placeholder becomes "Ask Google or type a
URL" (IDS_WEBUI_OMNIBOX_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT) instead of "Search Google or
type a URL". Update the expectations accordingly and remove the
overrides. The other disabled features are unchanged.

Verified locally: all OmniboxViewViewsPlaceholderTest tests pass (3x),

[omnibox][webui] Re-enable WebUI omnibox in ChromeOS tests

These tests disabled kWebUIOmniboxPopup and kWebUIOmniboxAimPopup as a
temporary workaround when the features were enabled by default
(crrev.com/c/8092074). The failures came from the hidden WebUI popup
WebContents that every browser window used to create at startup.
InProcessBrowserTest now creates those popups on demand
(crrev.com/c/8647556), so the overrides are no longer needed.

Verified with a CQ dry run of all such removals together
(crrev.com/c/8728211) and local repeat runs comparing the features
enabled vs. disabled, which showed no difference in failure rates.

[macOS] Scope network sandbox cache and support partition storage

When kTriggerNetworkDataMigration is enabled on macOS, the network
sandbox restricts file access to a subset of the user data and user
cache directories.

This change:
- Narrows user-cache-dir from granting access to the entire cache
  directory to only HTTP disk cache directories (root, profile, and
  Storage/ext/.../Cache).
- Grants user-data-dir access to Network and Shared Dictionary storage
  within extension partitions (Storage/ext/.../{Network, Shared
  Dictionary}), resolving unexpected sandbox denials.

[Actor] Support pinning opt-in notification in ActorForegroundService

When a remote experimental triggering opt-in request arrives on Android
while Chrome is in the background, the opt-in notification must be
pinned to ActorForegroundService so that the background session stays
alive until an Actor task starts or the opt-in request resolves or is
cancelled.

- Add pinOptInNotification, unpinOptInNotification,
  cancelOptInNotification, onServiceDestroyed, and hasOptInNotification
  in ActorForegroundServiceManager (building OPT_IN_NOTIFICATION_ID in
  processTaskUpdateQueue, clearing the opt-in state when replaced by a
  task notification, and cancelling it on shutDown and profile
  teardown).
- Handle ACTION_ACTOR_CANCEL without a task ID in ActorBroadcastReceiver
  via cancelOptInNotification and service teardown in
  ActorForegroundServiceImpl via onServiceDestroyed.
- Add unit tests in ActorForegroundServiceManagerTest covering opt-in
  notification pinning, cancellation via "No thanks", service and
  profile teardown, task transition, and pending-demotion priority.

[Clank][ImageWriter] (2/5) Use 512 KiB transfers on USB 3 drives

The Android write path moves the image in fixed-size chunks. Over USB,
each chunk is one SCSI WRITE (10) or READ (10) command, which takes
three USB transfers (command, data, status), each a Mojo round trip to
the device service. Chunks were 64 KiB, so a 4 GiB image took 65,536
commands to write and another 65,536 to verify.

Use 512 KiB chunks for USB 3 drives and for local block devices
(/dev/block). A 4 GiB image now takes 8,192 commands per pass (8x
fewer). USB 2.0 drives stay at 64 KiB.

Why USB 2.0 stays at 64 KiB: by default, Linux's own usb-storage driver
sends at most 240 sectors (120 KiB) per command to USB 2.0 drives,
because some older bridge chips fail near 256 sectors, but up to 2048
sectors (1 MiB) to USB 3 drives. Both of our sizes stay within what the
kernel itself sends to the same drive.

The speed comes from the bulk endpoints' wMaxPacketSize, which a device
reports for the speed it is actually running at: 1024 bytes on USB 3
and 512 bytes on USB 2.0. A USB 3 drive plugged into a USB 2.0 port
therefore also stays at 64 KiB.

On Linux/Android, usbfs (USBDEVFS_SUBMITURB) accepts multi-page bulk
URBs via scatter-gather up to the kernel's usbfs_memory_mb ceiling
(16 MiB by default). End-to-end physical hardware validation across
USB 3 and USB 2 ports/hubs is tracked in crbug.com/581068429.

Test: unit_tests --gtest_filter=*OperationAndroidUsbTest*:*ImageWriterFromFileTest*

Reland "[Glic] Track ClientLoadErrorReason for hidden and init load failures"

This is a reland of commit 2e08001200a9057a5a9ffd5c352c73559437b22f

Changes from original CL (in Patch Set 2):
- Guard HiddenInvokeFailsImmediatelyWhenClientNeedsSignIn and
  InactiveTabShowOnlyInvokeFailsWhenClientNeedsSignIn with
  GlicKeyedService::IsNoWebviewEnabled(GetProfile()) in this CL, since
  WebUI <webview> ClientLoadErrorReason reporting is wired in the
  follow-up reland CL (which removes the skip). Without GlicNoWebview
  (e.g. Android and branded ChromeOS builds that do not apply
  fieldtrial_testing_config.json), Host uses GlicWebUIContentsManager.

Original change's description:
> [Glic] Track ClientLoadErrorReason for hidden and init load failures
>
> Remote callers (ExperimentalTriggering) need per-session failure
> attribution on live terminal TaskUpdate responses when client loading
> fails. Client-side UMA/Structured Metrics are asynchronous and not
> joinable per wire session, and hidden invocations suppress
> NotifyClientLoadError so user-visible histograms are not polluted.
>
> Keep Host::client_load_error_reason() internal to
> //chrome/browser/glic:impl and track the active failure cause across
> all non-WebUI load failure paths:
> - Replace Host::SetClientLoadFailed(bool) with
>   Host::SetClientLoadFailed(ClientLoadErrorReason) and
>   Host::ClearClientLoadFailed().
> - Default to kClientError in Host::WebClientInitializeFailed() if no
>   prior cause was recorded, and wire GlicNoWebviewContentsManager to
>   report CurrentClientLoadErrorReason() (mapping
>   GuestState::kGuestError to kUnknown).
> - Clear client_load_error_reason_ in Host::HibernateImpl() so reloads
>   after hibernate never retain a stale cause.
> - Gate WaitForClientReadyTask's SignInBehavior and
>   GlicInvokeHandler::OnTimeout()'s kSignInRequired mapping on
>   instance.IsShowing() so hidden kSignIn failures fail immediately with
>   GlicInvokeError::kClientLoadError rather than waiting on an invisible
>   sign-in panel.
>
> WebUI <webview> client load failure reasons are wired in the next CL.
>
> Design doc:
> https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qqcCOq-g4rSIIUGRguIY9Tu8VpBVEazxBt2T8QsBpGc/edit
>
> Bug: b:579181811

[ash] token_handle_service: represent the session via User

Change TokenHandleService ctor to take a ChromeOS user session
user_manager::User instead of content::BrowserContext / Profile.

The factory resolves the User once, at construction time, via
BrowserContextHelper::GetUserByBrowserContext() -- the service
already relied on that same lookup internally, on every refresh
token notification. Prefs now come directly off
User::GetProfilePrefs(), and the account manager's path off
User::GetPath(). The service still derives a BrowserContext back,
via BrowserContextHelper::GetBrowserContextByUser(), at the one
remaining spot that needs a real BrowserContext API
(GetURLLoaderFactory()).

[browser_actuator] Bound SessionStreamRecorder entries and snapshots

When kBrowserActuatorInternals is enabled, SessionStreamRecorder retains
every entry in each session's entries_ vector without an upper bound,
and BuildEventSnapshot() serializes full binary payload fields into
Base64/JSON before truncating the formatted JSON string.

Long-running sessions can grow in-memory recording buffers without
bound, and Base64/JSON-encoding multi-megabyte proto payloads (such as
screenshots) before truncating causes unnecessary transient allocations
when building snapshots for chrome://browser-actuator-internals.

This CL caps per-session recorded entries at kMaxEntriesPerSession (256)
while computing SessionSnapshot::total_events from the uncapped metadata
counters, and truncates oversized proto payload value bytes to
max_message_bytes in BuildEventSnapshot() before serializing to JSON.

[Actor] Add opt-in notification builder in ActorNotificationFactory

When a remote experimental triggering opt-in request arrives on Android
while Chrome is in the background, Chrome needs a system notification on
the Actor channel so that tapping it opens a new tab with the pending
Actor task trigger extra, or tapping "No thanks" cancels the opt-in.

- Add ActorNotificationFactory.buildOptInNotification (with
  OPT_IN_NOTIFICATION_ID and both "Go to Chrome" and "No thanks"
  actions) and remove the unused-resource suppression from
  lint-suppressions.xml.
- Add ActorForegroundServiceController
  createTrustedPendingActorTaskNewTabIntent in
  ActorForegroundServiceControllerImpl and
  NoOpActorForegroundServiceController, and reuse it in
  LaunchIntentDispatcher.
- Add unit tests in ActorNotificationFactoryTest and
  ActorForegroundServiceControllerImplTest.

[Enterprise] Test disabled blocking in content analysis browser tests

In ContentAnalysisDelegateBlockingSettingBrowserTest, tests for
password-protected files, large files, and large pages previously
returned early when the corresponding blocking setting was disabled
(setting_param() is false).

When blocking settings are disabled, encrypted and large files are not
blocked client-side and are instead uploaded via the resumable upload
protocol, allowing the server verdict to determine the outcome. Update
BlockPasswordProtected and BlockLargeFiles to mock a successful scan
response from the server, verify that the action is allowed without an
unscanned file report, and assert the expected upload request and
acknowledgement counts. BlockPasswordProtected now waits for the
unscanned file report after the delegate finishes, like BlockLargeFiles.

Also remove the early return in BlockLargePages. With block_large_files
disabled, the page is sent to the upload service, which rejects it as
too large; the test now asserts the request and acknowledgement counts
for both setting values.

[iOS] Keep abandoned Cohort A3 profiles on disk during mapping cleanup

Instead of deleting the older initialized Managed profile in Cohort A3
during corrupted account-to-profile mapping cleanup
(crbug.com/577577657), archive its attributes in
prefs::kAbandonedProfiles and remove it from kProfileInfoCache without
marking its directory for deletion on disk.

If the associated managed account is later removed from the device,
move the abandoned profile to prefs::kProfilesToRemove so its directory
on disk is purged alongside active managed profiles.

[GPU]: Check largest swap chain in SwapChainTraceTest_IsOpaque

Under DelegatedCompositing on Windows, both the main WebContents
surface and smaller transparent browser WebUI surfaces (such as the
112x34 WebUIToolbar surface backed by a 128x64 swap chain) are
embedded child viz::Surface root passes that present as DXGI swap
chains. Because TraceIntegrationTest._IsSmallUiSwapChain only ignored
swap chains up to 64x64, the 128x64 / 112x34 WebUIToolbar swap chain
caused SwapChainTraceTest_IsOpaque to fail.

Instead of filtering by a hardcoded maximum UI swap chain size, update
_EvaluateSuccess_CheckSwapChainHasAlpha to evaluate the largest swap
chain (by dirty_rect area) so any smaller transparent WebUI surfaces
are ignored regardless of future size changes, and remove the
SwapChainTraceTest_IsOpaque failure expectations on Windows.

Remove decode request before running callback in ImageDecoderImpl

In ImageDecoderImpl::DecodeImageRequest, the completion callback was
previously invoked prior to removing the request from the decoder. If
the callback synchronously destroys the owning ImageDecoderImpl
instance (and with it `decode_image_requests_`), accessing `this` and
dereferencing `decoder_` after callback execution is a use-after-free.

This updates the cleanup sequence (and renames
RunCallbackAndRemoveRequest to RemoveRequestAndRunCallback) by moving
the callback to a local variable and calling RemoveDecodeImageRequest
before running the callback. A browser test is added to ensure teardown
can occur safely within the completion callback.

[BrowserActuator] Populate downstream type_url in SessionStreamRecorder

Downstream ActuatorDownstreamMessage envelopes delivered over the
transport stream do not always populate proto_payload.type_url on each
ActuatorDownstreamTypedPayload, whereas out-of-band FCM wake-up
envelopes synthesized in TransportSessionImpl::OnMessage() explicitly
set ExpectedTypeUrl(payload_type).

Because SessionStreamRecorder::RecordDownstreamMessage() stores
incoming envelopes verbatim, downstream payloads that arrive without a
populated type_url are recorded and exported to diagnostic dumps and
chrome://browser-actuator-internals with an empty
proto_payload.type_url, even when payload_type identifies a known
routable payload.

Backfill missing proto_payload.type_url fields in
SessionStreamRecorder::RecordDownstreamMessage() with
std::string(ExpectedTypeUrl(*payload_type)) whenever
FromDownstreamProtoPayloadType() resolves a known PayloadType, and add
unit test coverage in session_stream_recorder_unittest.cc.

[browser_actuator] Prune stopped active_tasks_ and guard OTR WebUI

ActuationTransportHandler inserts each started TaskId into active_tasks_
during OnStartTaskComplete() and only removes entries when
HandleStopTask() is explicitly called. In addition,
BrowserActuatorInternalsUIConfig::IsWebUIEnabled() checks the
kBrowserActuator and kBrowserActuatorInternals feature flags without
excluding null or off-the-record BrowserContexts.

When an ActorTask is stopped while PerformActions() is in flight (or
before it starts), OnActComplete() receives a non-OK
PerformActionsResponse with ActionResultCode::kTaskWentAway or
kUserNavigatedAway, yet the stopped TaskId remains in active_tasks_ for
the lifetime of the session and is passed to StopTask() again during
destructor cleanup. Allowing chrome://browser-actuator-internals in
Incognito or Guest profiles is also unnecessary because
TransportServiceFactory only supports regular profiles.

This CL removes stopped TaskIds from active_tasks_ in OnActComplete()
when action_status_code() indicates the task was already stopped
(kTaskWentAway or kUserNavigatedAway), while retaining active_tasks_
entries on recoverable action failures. It also requires a non-null,
non-off-the-record BrowserContext in
BrowserActuatorInternalsUIConfig::IsWebUIEnabled().

Remove the unused Variations.Limits.VariationKeySize.Large histogram.

Cast builds record the variations crash key size under .Large, but UMA
no longer processes Cast data and the histogram has received no data
since August 2024. Record it under .Default on all builds instead.

Cast still uses the larger 8 KiB crash key, since its child processes
fill this key and it still uploads crash reports.

parent
6b7c45030f62b75a5957dbeca5bc9d69a4673e2e [ diff ] 
[sharing_message] Add TransportService dependency to SharingService

SharingHandlerRegistryImpl registers BrowserActuatorMessageHandler
whenever browser_actuator::kBrowserActuator is enabled, passing the
Profile pointer without checking whether
browser_actuator::transport::TransportServiceFactory::GetForProfile()
returns a valid service. In addition, SharingServiceFactory does not
declare a DependsOn() edge on TransportServiceFactory.

Without an explicit KeyedService dependency edge, Profile destruction
order between SharingService and TransportService is not guaranteed by
DependencyManager, and registering BrowserActuatorMessageHandler on
profiles where GetForProfile(profile) returns nullptr (such as Guest or
off-the-record profiles) is unnecessary.

This CL adds
DependsOn(browser_actuator::transport::TransportServiceFactory::GetInstance())
in SharingServiceFactory, only registers BrowserActuatorMessageHandler
in SharingHandlerRegistryImpl when
TransportServiceFactory::GetForProfile(profile) is non-null, and
injects TransportService* directly into BrowserActuatorMessageHandler
instead of Profile*.

[Ozone] Mark confidential and OTR clipboard writes as secret on Linux

ClipboardOzone previously ignored the `privacy_types` bitmask passed to
`WritePortableAndPlatformRepresentations()`, causing passwords copied
via `ScopedClipboardWriter::MarkAsConfidential()` and Incognito copies
marked via `ScopedClipboardWriter::MarkAsOffTheRecord()` to be persisted
in plaintext by Linux clipboard managers (such as KDE Klipper, CopyQ,
GPaste, and wl-clipboard/cliphist) and mirroring copied passwords into
the X11/Wayland primary selection (`ClipboardBuffer::kSelection`,
middle-click paste).

Update `ClipboardOzone` to:
- Emit the `x-kde-passwordManagerHint` MIME/atom format with exact
  6-byte ASCII payload `"secret"` (no NUL terminator) whenever
  `kNoLocalClipboardHistory` or `kNoDisplay` is set in `privacy_types`.
- Skip mirroring `kCopyPaste` text into `kSelection` when `kNoDisplay`
  is set (`MarkAsConfidential()`), while preserving `kSelection`
  mirroring with `x-kde-passwordManagerHint` attached for
  off-the-record text copies (`kNoLocalClipboardHistory` without
  `kNoDisplay`).
- Pre-cache `x-kde-passwordManagerHint` in `x11::AtomCache` to avoid a
  synchronous X11 `InternAtom` round-trip on first confidential copy.

Also fix `SelectionData::TakeBytes()` in `ui/base/x/selection_utils.cc`
to move `memory_` instead of calling `scoped_refptr::release()`, which
previously leaked the underlying `RefCountedMemory` reference on every
`X11ClipboardOzone::RequestClipboardData()` read.

Reserve capacity for proc maps regions on Linux

Pre-allocates capacity in the regions vector based on the number of
lines to avoid unnecessary reallocations while parsing /proc/self/maps.

These were reported to be some of the biggest unreserved vectors in the
Chromium codebase, peaking at >10,000+ entries.

Also hoisted the check for the last, empty line out of the loop,
simplifying it and reducing the amount of work done.
